bridge_title: The Bridge: your library, spoken in Lantern
bridge_lede: A gateway that presents an Ownfoil or AeroFoil server, a Tinfoil shop or plain folders of games as a Lantern server, so that Lantern clients can browse it, download from it and sync with it.

bridge_how_lede: A library the clients already understand, with none of the work on their side.
bridge_how_1_x: Lantern asks for the SHA-256 of every file. With the games mounted read-only, the bridge hashes them on disk and serves them itself; a slower remote mode hashes what it downloads, once.
bridge_how_2_x: Everything the SDK's server toolkit does: pairing with a code or a QR code, device-bound tokens, invitations, a rating cap carried by the token.
bridge_how_3_x: The state of the sources and of the hashing queue, the devices to approve, live logs and the configuration.

faq_1_q: Does the bridge change my library?
faq_1_a: Your games are only read, where they are: mount the folders read-only. The one thing it writes back is AeroFoil's saves and cheats, when a Lantern client sends them. Everything else it keeps is its own settings, index and history, in its configuration folder.
faq_2_q: Where do my shop passwords go?
faq_2_a: Not into the configuration file: it holds only the name of an environment variable, and the bridge reads the password from the environment. A backup contains no secret.
faq_3_a: Operators you create, each with one of four roles: the first owner is made with a one-time setup code, and others may come in through your sign-in proxy or provider. By default only the local network can reach the pages, wrong passwords are counted per address and per name, a session ends after 30 idle minutes, and the pages load nothing from elsewhere.
faq_4_q: Does it contact anything outside my network?
faq_4_a: Two checks are on by default and each can be turned off: a daily download of Atlas's public list of games, and a daily look at GitHub's latest release. Both are plain requests: nothing about your library is sent and nothing is installed.
faq_5_a: Only devices you have paired: a new device enters a code made with the invite command, and until then only the handshake is open. Letting anyone read it is a setting, not recommended outside a network you trust.
accounts_lede: Several people can run the bridge, and each player gets an account with only the rights you choose. It is all on the administration pages, and from a terminal on a machine without a browser. The names below are made up.
acc_ops_x: Four fixed roles: owner, administrator, manager (for a parent who looks after the family's consoles) and read-only. The server checks the role on every request, not only in the menu.
acc_players_x: Full, Child (no cheats, with an age limit) or Guest (the library only), or right by right. Freeze an account, or delete it with everything kept for it.
acc_consoles_x: Give it a name, take rights away, set an age limit of its own, suspend it for a while or revoke it. When a console pairs, compare its key's fingerprint with the console's own before you approve.
acc_signin_x: Let people in through an authentication proxy (Authelia, Authentik…) or an OpenID Connect provider: their groups give their role. Every change is a line of the journal that says who made it.
